children: UFBU backs the November 2–3 protest over the proposed Fairfax deal, citing concerns over public ownership and employee safeguards

IDBI Bank employees are set to stage a two-day nationwide strike on November 2 and 3, opposing the proposed sale of the bank to Canadian investor Fairfax Financial Holdings, with the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) extending support to the agitation.

In a circular dated October 22, the UFBU urged its affiliated unions and members to participate in solidarity programmes, backing the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees’ campaign against the proposed sale of a 60% stake held by the government and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC).

The UFBU has questioned the proposed transfer of ownership and management control to a foreign investor, arguing that it raises concerns over the bank’s public-sector character. It has also cited a parliamentary assurance made in 2003 that the government would retain at least a 51% stake in IDBI.

The employee forum has demanded that the government halt the transaction and acquire an additional 6% equity in the bank, either from LIC or through market purchases, to maintain majority ownership. It has also sought written assurances that existing service conditions, welfare measures, pension benefits and reservation policies will be protected, along with the continuation of industry-level wage revisions.
As part of its solidarity campaign, the UFBU has called for participation in demonstrations and a social media campaign, besides other protest activities ahead of the strike.

The proposed agitation comes as the government moves to divest its stake in IDBI Bank, a lender that the unions say has returned to profitability in recent years. The strike is intended to press for a reconsideration of the proposed transaction and safeguards for employees.
